name: KYC Verification Process
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for Know Your Customer (KYC) verification at FirstUK Bank, governed by the Compliance department and effective from 2026-01-15.

name: Head of Compliance
description: The designated owner of the KYC Verification SOP responsible for oversight and ownership of the procedure.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Personnel within the Compliance department who are the target audience for and executors of the KYC verification procedures.
context: Audience | Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, Operations

name: Branch Staff
description: Front-line personnel responsible for the initial execution and application of the KYC verification process.
context: Audience | Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, Operations

name: Operations Staff
description: Operational personnel involved in the processing and administration of the KYC verification workflow.
context: Audience | Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, Operations

name: KYC Verification Process
description: A procedure to confirm customer identity and address during account opening and at periodic intervals. The process ensures institutional compliance with FCA COBS Part 10 and Money Laundering Regulations 2017.
context: Establish procedures for conducting Know Your Customer (KYC) verification to confirm customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter
ensuring compliance with FCA COBS Part 10 and Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: Customer Account Opening and Re-verification Process
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for opening accounts for new customers and performing periodic re-verification based on risk schedules. This process applies across all banking channels, including branch, online, and postal, and requires verification for all joint account holders.
context: Applies to: All customer account openings (new customers)

name: New Customer
description: The individual applying for a new account who is the subject of the account opening process.

name: Joint Account Holder
description: Individuals opening a joint account who are both required to undergo the verification process.

name: New Customer Account
description: The account being established for a new customer as part of the opening process.

name: Joint Account
description: An account arrangement involving multiple holders, where the SOP specifies that both parties must complete verification.

name: KYC Verification Process
description: An end-to-end operational workflow to verify customer identity and address, assess risk, and record data. The process typically concludes within 1–2 business days.

name: Document Collection
description: The initial stage of the KYC process where necessary identification documents are gathered from the customer.

name: Document Verification
description: The stage where the collected identification documents are checked for authenticity and validity.

name: Address Verification
description: The stage dedicated to confirming the customer's residential address using provided evidence.

name: Risk Assessment
description: An evaluative stage where the customer's risk profile is determined based on the verified information.

name: System Recording
description: The stage where verified customer data and risk assessments are entered into the bank's official systems.

name: Quality Check
description: A final review stage to ensure all previous KYC steps were completed accurately and in accordance with standards.

name: KYC Approval Gate
description: The final decision point determining if the KYC process is successfully completed or if it must be escalated due to failure.

name: KYC Compliance Checkpoint
description: The mandatory regulatory gate verifying that all KYC steps (Collection, Verification, Risk Assessment) have been satisfied before approval.

name: Customer
description: The individual providing the necessary information and documentation to undergo the KYC verification process.

name: Customer Identity Document Collection Process
description: The operational procedure for requesting and collecting valid photo identification from customers to satisfy identity requirements. It specifies acceptable primary documents and explicitly lists unacceptable forms of ID.

name: Identity Document Request Step
description: The initial action of requesting a valid form of photo identification from the customer. The staff must specifically ask for a UK Passport or Driving License.
context: Please provide a valid form of photo identification (UK Passport or Driving License)

name: Bank Staff Member
description: The employee responsible for executing the document request and verifying the validity of the provided identification documents.
context: Please provide a valid form of photo identification

name: Customer Applicant
description: The individual providing photo identification to the bank for verification purposes.
context: Please provide a valid form of photo identification

name: UK Passport
description: An acceptable primary identification document. It must be valid (not expired), have a clear photo page, and all security features must be visible.

name: UK Driving License
description: An acceptable primary identification document, provided it is in photocard format, valid, contains a visible signature, and has an intact driving record.

name: Document Validity and Acceptability Gate
description: A check to determine if the provided document is acceptable. Documents are rejected if they are expired, damaged, illegible, provisional, or non-UK (without secondary verification).
context: Non-UK documents (unless verified via secondary source)

name: Address Document Request Process
description: The procedure for requesting and verifying a customer's current address using a set of approved primary and secondary documentation. It defines the specific documents acceptable to the bank for address confirmation.
context: Please provide a document confirming your current address

name: Address Document Collection
description: The initial stage of the process where the bank requests a document from the customer to confirm their current residency.
context: Please provide a document confirming your current address

name: Address Document Verification
description: The review process where submitted documents are checked against the list of primary (dated within 3 months) and secondary acceptable documents.

name: Customer
description: The individual responsible for providing the requested address confirmation documents to the bank.
context: Please provide a document confirming your current address

name: Address Validation Checkpoint
description: The compliance gate where a submitted document is validated as either a Primary document (requiring a date within 3 months) or a Secondary document.

name: Primary Address Evidence
description: High-validity address documents that must be dated within 3 months, including Utility Bills, Council Tax Documents, Bank Statements, and Mortgage Statements.
context: Council Tax Document (Bill or banding notice)

name: Secondary Address Evidence
description: Alternative address evidence that may be used, including tenancy agreements, insurance policies, HMRC letters, and electoral register extracts.

name: Document Verification Process
description: An in-branch procedure for verifying the authenticity and validity of a customer's physical identity documents. It involves physical examination, photo and signature comparison, and data recording to ensure the customer is who they claim to be.

name: Original Document Examination
description: The initial physical inspection of the original identity document. The actor must verify security features, watermarks, and ensure the document has not been tampered with.

name: Photo Comparison Step
description: A visual verification step where the photo on the provided identification document is compared against the customer's actual appearance to ensure a match.
context: Compare photo on ID to customer's appearance

name: Signature Verification Step
description: A consistency check comparing the signature found on the identity document with the signature provided by the customer on the application form.
context: Compare signature on ID to customer's signature on form

name: Document Expiry Check
description: A validation step to confirm that the identity document is current and has not expired, including noting the expiry date in the bank's records.

name: Document Data Recording
description: The administrative step of logging the document type, number, issue date, and expiry date, while specifying the verification method as 'in-branch examination'.
context: Record issue date and expiry date

name: Branch Staff
description: The bank personnel responsible for conducting the physical examination of documents, comparing IDs to the customer, and recording the data in the system.

name: Document Validity and Authenticity Gate
description: A decision point based on a set of pass/fail criteria including document expiration, photo/signature matches, and physical integrity. Failure to meet any criteria (e.g., expired document or identity mismatch) results in a fail outcome.
context: Pass Criteria: Document valid and not expired

name: Physical Identity Verification Checkpoint
description: The mandatory control point where the result of the physical document examination is verified. The workflow only proceeds if all pass criteria (validity, photo match, signature match, and security features) are satisfied.

name: Customer
description: The individual seeking to open an account or perform a transaction who must provide original identity documents and be physically present for comparison.
context: Compare photo on ID to customer's appearance
Compare signature on ID to customer's signature on form

name: Identity Document
description: Official identification provided by the customer, specifically referencing Passports and Driving Licenses, which are checked for security features and expiration.
context: Compare photo on ID to customer's appearance

name: Address Verification Process
description: An operational procedure to verify a customer's residential address using identity documents and secondary evidence. The process ensures the address is within the UK, follows the correct postcode format, and is supported by current documentation.
context: Confirm address is in United Kingdom

name: Address Format Check
description: The initial check to ensure the customer's address is located within the United Kingdom and conforms to the specific UK postcode format A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2). Any concerns regarding the address must be noted.
context: Confirm address is in United Kingdom

name: Address Document Matching
description: A comparative analysis between the address listed on the primary identity document and the secondary supporting document. If discrepancies are found, the actor must investigate potential causes such as spelling variances or recent moves.
context: Compare address on ID with address on secondary document
If addresses differ: Investigate (recent move? spelling variance?)

name: Document Currency Validation
description: The process of checking the validity dates of secondary documents. Utility bills and bank statements must be dated within 3 months, tenancy agreements must be signed/current, and insurance policies must be active.
context: Utility bill, council tax: Dated within 3 months
Tenancy agreement: Must be signed and current
Insurance policy: Must be active policy

name: Address Verification Pass/Fail Gate
description: A final decision point to determine if the address verification is successful based on four criteria: matching addresses, UK location, document currency (within 3 months), and valid postcode format.
context: Address on ID matches secondary document

name: Address Validity Compliance Checkpoint
description: The formal control gate where the bank verifies that the residency obligations have been met before the onboarding or update process can advance.
context: Pass Criteria: ✅ Address on ID matches secondary document

name: Secondary Address Document
description: Supporting documentation used to verify the customer's address, subject to specific currency requirements (e.g., 3 months for bills/statements).
context: Utility bill, council tax: Dated within 3 months
Tenancy agreement: Must be signed and current
Insurance policy: Must be active policy

name: Customer Residential Address
description: The physical address of the customer being verified, which must be located in the UK and match across provided documents.
context: Confirm address is in United Kingdom
Compare address on ID with address on secondary document

name: Risk Assessment Process
description: The procedure for determining a customer's risk category based on residency, age, product type, address, PEP status, and deposit value.

name: Customer Risk Level Determination
description: The action of assessing customer attributes against defined criteria to assign a risk rating of Low, Medium, or High.

name: Risk Category Classification Gate
description: A branching decision point where customers are categorized as Low, Medium, or High risk based on specific flags such as residency, PEP status, and account value.

name: PEP and Adverse Media Screening Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance check to identify Politically Exposed Persons or adverse media flags, which triggers a High Risk classification.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A standard banking product identified as a factor for Low Risk categorization.

name: Current Account
description: A standard banking product identified as a factor for Low Risk categorization.

name: Low Risk Customer
description: A customer profile meeting criteria such as UK residency, age 18-65, and no PEP flags.

name: Medium Risk Customer
description: A customer profile characterized by non-UK residency in developed countries or higher-value accounts (>£50k).

name: High Risk Customer
description: A customer profile meeting high-risk criteria including PEP status, adverse media, or residency in countries with weak AML controls.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Process
description: An operational workflow triggered for high-risk customers requiring additional verification and senior management approval before an account can be created.
context: If High-Risk: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence

name: Mark Customer for Enhanced Due Diligence
description: The initial action of flagging a customer as high-risk to initiate the EDD workflow.
context: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence

name: Escalate to Compliance Head
description: The act of moving the customer file to the Compliance Head for review due to high-risk status.

name: Perform Additional Verification
description: Conducting deeper checks into the customer's profile, specifically targeting beneficial ownership and source of funds.
context: Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior official responsible for reviewing high-risk escalations and providing the final approval for account creation.
context: Compliance Head approval required before account creation

name: High-Risk Status Determination
description: A branching point where the process diverts to EDD if the customer is identified as High-Risk.

name: Compliance Head Approval Gate
description: A critical approval gate where the Compliance Head must authorize the process before an account can be created.
context: Compliance Head approval required before account creation

name: Beneficial Ownership and Source of Funds Check
description: A mandatory compliance verification of the customer's ownership structure and the origin of their funds.
context: Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer identified as high-risk who is the subject of the Enhanced Due Diligence process.
context: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence

name: New Account
description: The account intended for creation following the successful completion and approval of the EDD process.
context: Compliance Head approval required before account creation

name: System Recording
description: The stage of the process where verified customer identification, address details, and risk assessment data are formally entered into the Account Management System (AMS). It ensures all verification metadata is captured for audit and compliance purposes.

name: AMS Staff Member
description: The bank staff member responsible for performing the verification and recording their name or ID in the AMS system to attest to the validity of the documents.

name: Identity Document Verification Recording
description: A control point where the system records the specific identity document used (Passport or Driving License), its validity dates, and the method of verification used to ensure the identity check is satisfied.
context: Verification Method (In-branch examination / Online upload / Postal)

name: Address Verification Recording
description: A mandatory recording gate that captures the customer's registered or correspondence address along with the specific evidence document (e.g., Utility Bill) used to verify the residency.
context: Document Type (Utility Bill / Council Tax / etc.)

name: Risk Assessment Entry
description: The final checkpoint in the recording process where the customer is assigned a risk level and determined if Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required, including the scheduling of the next review date.

name: EDD Requirement Decision
description: A branching point where the staff must decide if the customer requires Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) based on the risk assessment, necessitating a recorded reason if flagged 'Yes'.

name: Identity Document
description: Official identity documents used for verification, specifically Passports and Driving Licenses, requiring the recording of document numbers and expiry dates.

name: Customer Address
description: The physical residence or correspondence address of the customer, captured as part of the AMS entry process.

name: KYC Quality Check and Approval Process
description: A quality assurance workflow to verify that all KYC documentation and risk assessments are complete and accurate before final approval. It involves a detailed checklist and manager sign-off.

name: KYC Documentation and Risk Verification
description: A comprehensive review of collected identity documents, address verification, photo matching, and risk assessment completion. All data must be recorded in the AMS system.
context: Identity document collected and verified (original or certified copy)

name: Manager Sign-Off and Filing
description: The final review phase where an authorized manager evaluates the checklist and either approves the KYC or requests more information, followed by filing the checklist in the account record.
context: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: Operations Manager
description: A management role responsible for reviewing the KYC verification quality checklist and providing final approval or requesting further evidence.
context: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: Compliance Staff
description: A role dedicated to ensuring regulatory requirements are met by reviewing the quality checklist and authorizing the KYC process.
context: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: KYC Approval Gate
description: A critical decision point where the manager determines if the KYC verification is sufficient for approval or if additional documentation is required.

name: KYC Pre-Approval Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory control point ensuring all identity, address, and risk assessment requirements (including EDD if applicable) are satisfied before the account can proceed.

name: KYC Subject
description: The individual whose identity and address are being verified against provided documentation and photo evidence.

name: Customer Account Record
description: The system record where the final signed-off KYC quality checklist is archived.

name: Identity Document
description: Official identification provided by the customer, which must be original or a certified copy and not expired.
context: Identity document collected and verified (original or certified copy)

name: Proof of Address Document
description: A secondary document used to verify the customer's residence, which must be current and dated within the last 3 months.

name: Periodic Re-Verification Process
description: A risk-based operational workflow to re-verify customer information at set intervals or upon specific triggers. The frequency of verification is determined by the customer's risk rating (Low, Medium, or High).

name: Low-Risk Customer Re-Verification
description: Re-verification of customers classified as low-risk occurring every 5 years. This process is initiated by an automatic system reminder and may be waived if no risk increase is indicated.
context: May be waived if customer activity indicates no risk increase

name: Medium-Risk Customer Re-Verification
description: Re-verification of customers classified as medium-risk occurring every 3 years. Includes ongoing monitoring via quarterly risk assessments.

name: High-Risk Customer Re-Verification
description: Annual re-verification for high-risk customers. This step involves quarterly enhanced monitoring and a transaction-by-transaction review to identify suspicious patterns.

name: Immediate Re-Verification Trigger Check
description: A decision gate that triggers an immediate re-verification process regardless of the scheduled cycle if specific event-based triggers occur, such as address changes or fraud alerts.

name: Automated System
description: The banking system responsible for automatically generating reminders for the re-verification of low-risk customers.

name: Low-Risk Customer
description: Customers classified as low-risk who are subject to a 5-year re-verification cycle.

name: Medium-Risk Customer
description: Customers classified as medium-risk who are subject to a 3-year re-verification cycle and quarterly assessments.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customers classified as high-risk requiring annual re-verification and enhanced monitoring.

name: Risk Classification Check
description: The control point where a customer's risk level (Low, Medium, High) is determined to assign the correct re-verification frequency and monitoring intensity.

name: Customer Address Update
description: The action of a customer registering a new address, which serves as a trigger for immediate re-verification.

name: Fraud Alert Trigger
description: A fraud detection event that necessitates the immediate re-verification of the customer's status.

name: Sanctions List Hit
description: A match found during sanctions screening that triggers an immediate re-verification process.

name: Re-Verification Process
description: A procedure to refresh customer verification data, mirroring the initial verification steps. It involves contacting the customer for updated documentation and updating the system records.

name: Customer Document Request Step
description: The action of contacting the customer to request updated identity or address documents as part of the re-verification workflow.

name: Document Verification and System Update Step
description: The stage where the provided updated documents are verified for authenticity and the customer's system records are updated accordingly.

name: Re-verification Date Recording Step
description: The final administrative action of recording the date the re-verification was completed within the bank's systems.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who is the subject of the re-verification process and is responsible for providing updated documentation.

name: Online KYC Verification Process
description: The end-to-end digital procedure for verifying a customer's identity and address during online account opening. The timeline is less than 1 hour for automated paths and 1–2 business days for manual reviews.
context: Timeline: < 1 hour (if no issues), 1–2 business days (if manual review)

name: Digital Document Upload and Initial Review
description: The initial stage where the customer uploads identification and the system or compliance staff performs a verification check.
context: Customer uploads photo of ID (Passport or Driving License)

name: Document Verification Detail Check
description: A detailed review of the uploaded ID to ensure the document is not expired, the number format is correct, and the image quality is sufficient.

name: Address Verification Step
description: The process of validating the customer's address through form entry, automated postcode verification, and potential secondary document upload reviewed by staff.

name: KYC Approval Decision
description: The final review step where compliance staff either approve the KYC submission or request further clarification from the customer.
context: Compliance staff approves or requests clarification
If approved, account proceeds to AML screening

name: Compliance Staff
description: Human actors responsible for performing manual reviews of uploaded documents and addresses, as well as making the final approval or rejection decision.
context: Compliance staff approves or requests clarification

name: Automated Verification System
description: The system component that performs automated ID verification and postcode validation.

name: Customer
description: The individual applying for an account who provides identification and address details via the digital interface.

name: KYC Approval Gate
description: A decision point where the submission is either approved (leading to AML screening) or rejected (leading to customer notification).
context: Compliance staff approves or requests clarification
If approved, account proceeds to AML screening

name: Manual Review Trigger
description: A condition where an unclear image or automated failure triggers a manual review by compliance staff.
context: Flag for manual review if unclear

name: KYC Compliance Checkpoint
description: The mandatory gate verifying that identity and address requirements have been satisfied before the workflow is permitted to advance to AML screening.
context: If approved, account proceeds to AML screening

name: Identity Document
description: Official identification provided by the customer, specifically listed as a Passport or Driving License.
context: Customer uploads photo of ID (Passport or Driving License)

name: Customer Address
description: The residential address provided by the customer, verified via postcode and potentially secondary documentation.

name: Postal KYC Verification
description: An operational workflow for verifying customer identity and address via certified postal documents. The process involves third-party certification and internal bank review with a total timeline of 3–5 business days.

name: Customer Document Submission
description: The initial stage where the customer provides certified copies of their identification and address documentation, specifically notarized by a solicitor or notary public.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Third Party Document Certification
description: The process performed by a solicitor or notary public to verify the customer's identity, confirm the document is a genuine copy, and apply a dated stamp and signature.

name: Bank Certification Review
description: The internal bank review where operations staff verify the certifier's details and record the verification in the system.

name: Customer
description: The individual undergoing the KYC process who is responsible for providing certified identification and address documents.

name: Solicitor or Notary Public
description: An external professional responsible for verifying the customer's identity, confirming document authenticity, and signing/stamping the certification.

name: Operations Staff
description: Bank personnel responsible for reviewing the certifications, confirming the legitimacy of the certifier, and recording the result in the bank's system.

name: Certifier Verification Trigger
description: A decision point where operations staff determine if there are concerns regarding the certification that necessitate direct contact with the solicitor or notary public.
context: May contact certifier to verify (if concerns)

name: Postal Document Compliance Gate
description: The mandatory control point where the bank verifies that the identity and address documents have been correctly certified by an approved professional before recording the KYC status.

name: Certified Identity Document
description: A copy of the customer's identity document that must be notarized by a solicitor or notary public.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Certified Address Document
description: A document used to verify the customer's residential address, required to be provided as a certified copy.

name: Escalation & Exceptions Procedure
description: A procedure defining the specific triggers and criteria that require a customer verification case to be escalated to senior compliance management for review.

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior authority responsible for reviewing escalated cases involving identity discrepancies, potential fraud, or high-risk customer profiles.

name: Level 2 — Compliance Head Review
description: An escalation tier where the Compliance Head evaluates exceptions and high-risk triggers that cannot be resolved at the frontline level.

name: Identity and Risk Escalation Trigger
description: A decision gate determining whether to proceed with standard onboarding or escalate to the Compliance Head based on ID validity, address matching, or risk status.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer categorized as high-risk due to being a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or having associated adverse media, requiring escalation.

name: Exception Process
description: The operational workflow for handling account application exceptions, involving documentation, escalation to the Compliance Head, and a final decision on the application.

name: Exception Reason Documentation
description: The initial step in the exception process where the specific reason for the exception is formally documented.

name: Escalation to Compliance Head
description: The action of moving the exception case up to the Compliance Head for review and decision making.

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior official responsible for reviewing exception cases and deciding whether to approve, request more info, or reject an account application.

name: Compliance Review and Decision
description: The stage where the Compliance Head evaluates the exception and selects one of three possible outcomes.

name: Exception Approval Gate
description: A branching point where the Compliance Head decides to either approve the application with conditions, request alternative verification, or reject the account application.

name: Decision System Recording
description: The final step where the decision reached by the Compliance Head is formally recorded in the system.

name: Account Applicant
description: The individual whose account application is subject to the exception process and potentially denied based on the decision.

name: Proposed Account
description: The new account application being processed through the exception workflow.

name: Staff Training and Competency Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for ensuring staff are trained and certified in document authentication, customer communication, data entry, and compliance procedures. It includes a knowledge assessment and practical observation.

name: Document Authentication Training
description: Training staff on how to identify counterfeit documents and recognise legitimate security features.

name: Customer Communication Training
description: Instruction on how to clearly explain the bank's Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements to customers.

name: System Data Entry Training
description: Training to ensure accurate recording of customer information into the bank's systems.

name: Compliance Procedures Training
description: Training regarding the specific compliance rules and the criteria for when a matter must be escalated.

name: Knowledge Assessment
description: A formal test that staff must pass as part of their certification process.

name: Practical Observation Assessment
description: A practical evaluation where a manager observes the staff member processing at least 5 customers to verify competency.
context: Practical observation (verified by manager on 5+ customers)

name: Annual Refresher Training
description: Mandatory yearly training to maintain staff competency and updated knowledge of procedures.

name: Staff Member
description: The personnel undergoing training and certification in operational and compliance procedures.

name: Manager
description: The individual responsible for verifying a staff member's competency through practical observation of customer interactions.

name: Certification Approval Gate
description: A decision point where staff must pass both the knowledge assessment and the practical observation to be certified.
context: Practical observation (verified by manager on 5+ customers)

name: Account Opening Process
description: The operational workflow for opening a new account, which incorporates KYC as a primary component (specifically Step 3).

name: KYC Step in Account Opening
description: The third discrete action within the Account Opening Process dedicated to Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures.

name: Head of Compliance
description: The individual responsible for authoring and updating the operational procedure documents, including version 1.0 and 2.0.

name: Head of Compliance
description: The senior official responsible for the final approval and sign-off of the operational procedure on 2026-01-15.
context: Approved by: Head of Compliance — Date: 2026-01-15

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: The executive officer responsible for the final approval and sign-off of the operational procedure on 2026-01-15.
